lines.text: Eliphaz the Temanite says Job once steadied those who stumbled, but now trouble has come upon him.
Eliphaz asks who innocent has ever perished, and says those who sow trouble perish by the sword of their enemies.
A spirit glided past Eliphaz in a night vision, and its whispering voice asked if a mortal can be more righteous than God.
Eliphaz says a fool's house is cursed, his sons have a defender in court, and the hungry consume his harvest.

wrong_details.wrong: his sons have a defender in court
wrong_details.true: his sons are crushed in court without a defender

lines.text: Eliphaz says he would bring his cause before God, who wounds and also binds, and promises Job many offspring.
